_comment: NARRATIVE DIVERSITY pane. No numbers or statistics are shown here by design. All three axes are wired to real clips. Animation Style plays one diagram (CVPR_2025_pipe00041) rendered in all five Layer 1 styles, so the styles are compared on identical content. Pan and Zoom is Layer 2: it is a toggle rather than a sixth style, it composes on whichever Layer 1 style is selected, and it plays the animation itself (an SVG under assets/bench/pan_and_zoom/) rather than a clip - see data/benchmark/pan-and-zoom.json, which tools/build_pan_and_zoom.py generates. The other two axes play one example per variant, assembled from that variant's own rendered frames and its own narration.

categories.label: Animation Style diversity
categories.blurb: Five base styles decide how a diagram's elements are revealed

variants.label: Alpha Masking
variants.caption: Elements dissolve in behind a soft alpha mask.

variants.label: Colour Pop
variants.caption: The page stays desaturated; the live element regains its colour.

variants.label: Hopping Bbox
variants.caption: A highlight box jumps from element to element.

variants.label: Progressive Reveal
variants.caption: The figure builds up one beat at a time, never erasing.

variants.label: Sliding Bbox
variants.caption: The highlight glides along the path the process takes.

variants.label: Pan and Zoom
variants.caption: The camera travels the figure, holding on each element as it is described.

categories.layer2Note: Layer 2 pan and zoom composes on top of any of them

categories.label: Presentation Sequence Length
categories.blurb: How finely the planner cuts the process up. The same figure can carry a handful of decisive steps or one step per element.

variants.label: Fast reveal
variants.caption: The process moves in large strides; several elements arrive together.

variants.label: Medium reveal
variants.caption: One stage of the method per step, start to finish.

variants.label: Element by element
variants.hint: every element, one at a time
variants.caption: Every element gets its own step, so nothing arrives unannounced.

categories._note: The clips run at 4x. Their pacing was the narration’s, and this axis carries no narration on the page, so at 1x the stage was holding a still for seconds at a time with nothing to read.

categories.blurb: How much is said at each step, from a caption-length cue to a full spoken explanation of the mechanism.

beats.text: The memory architecture is divided into User Space and Kernel Space.
In User Space, execution begins at the Database Process.
The process initiates an asynchronous write call.
This is followed by a synchronous fsync operation.
The write call routes into the Page Cache within Kernel Space and returns immediately, creating dirty pages.
The Kernel Flusher Thread periodically handles writebacks from the Page Cache.
Requests pass into the I/O Queue, while fsync waits for disk completion.
At the bottom is Persistent Storage, containing the Block Device.
Finally, enqueued operations are flushed from the I/O Queue down to the Block Device.
The diagram introduces key architectural conventions, including average aggregation, depthwise convolutions, and trainable scaling parameters.
In the Swin-Transformer block, input features pass through layer normalization alongside an initial residual shortcut.
Normalized features enter the window and shifted-window multi-head self-attention module to capture spatial context.
The attention outputs are then merged with the initial residual connection.
The first Mona adapter layer processes the aggregated representation to enhance visual feature adaptation.
Features undergo a second layer normalization step before the feed-forward network, accompanied by another skip connection.
A feed-forward layer then transforms the intermediate token representations.
The feed-forward output is summed with its corresponding shortcut.
A second Mona layer further refines the features before outputting the final representation of the Swin-Transformer block.
Inside the Mona layer, input features undergo layer normalization scaled by a trainable factor, while a parallel skip branch is scaled by a second factor.
The scaled feature streams are combined at an addition node to regulate input distribution.
A down projection layer reduces channel dimensionality before branching into multi-scale convolutional paths and residual shortcuts.
Three parallel depthwise convolutions with 3x3, 5x5, and 7x7 kernels extract multi-scale visual patterns.
Outputs from all three kernel branches are combined using an averaging operation.
The averaged depthwise feature is added to the pre-convolution residual branch.
A 1x1 convolution aggregates point-wise channel features alongside an adjacent residual shortcut.
The 1x1 convolution output is summed with its shortcut connection.
A GeLU activation function introduces non-linearity.
An up projection layer restores the original feature channel dimensions.
Finally, the outer residual is added to yield the complete output of the Mona layer.
The pipeline begins with the editing guidance generation stage to convert user edits into supervision signals that can later guide the model during training.

A pretrained teacher model encapsulates the original neural radiance field of the reconstructed scene. It therefore provides a reliable reference that can be queried to determine what the edited scene should look like.

When a user interactively edits a region, such as scaling an object, a spatial mapping function is established, which helps to understand the relationship between the edited space and the original scene.
Sampled points and ray directions in the edited target space are mapped back to the source space, querying the teacher model to obtain color and density guidance.
This generated guidance is then transferred to a two-stage student training framework designed for instant preview.

A local loss focuses specifically on the edited object or region, ensuring that the requested modification is learned correctly. At the same time, a global loss considers the scene as a whole, helping the model maintain consistency with everything outside the edited region.
During local pretraining, only local feature parameters are updated while decoder weights remain frozen, enabling instant preview within one second.

In the second stage, global fine-tuning refines the entire scene network using full supervision from teacher inference, allowing the model to adjust both the edited region and the surrounding scene for a more consistent and fully converged result.
The resulting student model delivers fully converged, high-fidelity rendering of the edited 3D scene.

categories._note: Each variant carries its own narration, timed to its clip, and the pane shows the line being spoken under the stage. That is the axis: a side label saying "a sentence per step" describes the difference, the narration itself IS the difference. These clips play at 1x for the same reason.
